title: Number Sentences: Writing and Solving
seo_title: Grade 4 Number Sentences Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Write number sentences to describe problem situations; solve and complete number sentences by inspection and trial and improvement; check solutions by substitution.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 4 number sentences worksheets: fact families, unknowns, the equal sign, trial and improvement and writing number sentences. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: = means both sides have the same value.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A number sentence uses numbers and signs: 25 + ☐ = 60.
  • The equal sign means both sides have the same value.
  • Solve by inspection (just see it) or by trial and improvement: try a number, check, and improve.
  • Write a number sentence for a problem, solve it, and check by substitution: put the answer back in.

Examples

Example

☐ × 6 = 54

try 8: 48, too small

try 9: 54

Answer: 9

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
One side's answerIn 25 + ☐ = 30 + 15, ☐ is 20, not 45.
= means the answer= means the same value.
Wrong orderFollow the story.

items.q: 45 + 38 = 83. Which subtraction fact is in the same fact family?
items.e: A fact family uses the same three numbers. In a subtraction fact, the whole (83) comes first: 83 − 45 = 38 and 83 − 38 = 45.

items.q: 160 + 240 = 400. Which subtraction fact is in the same fact family?
items.e: A fact family uses the same three numbers. In a subtraction fact, the whole (400) comes first: 400 − 160 = 240 and 400 − 240 = 160.

items.q: 275 + 325 = 600. Which subtraction fact is in the same fact family?
items.e: A fact family uses the same three numbers. In a subtraction fact, the whole (600) comes first: 600 − 275 = 325 and 600 − 325 = 275.

items.q: 318 + 482 = 800. Which subtraction fact is in the same fact family?
items.e: A fact family uses the same three numbers. In a subtraction fact, the whole (800) comes first: 800 − 318 = 482 and 800 − 482 = 318.

items.q: Which number sentence is in the same fact family as 500 − 180 = 320?
items.e: Addition is the inverse of subtraction. 500 − 180 = 320, so 320 + 180 = 500. 500 + 180 = 680 is true, but it does not use 500, 180 and 320.

items.q: Which number sentence is in the same fact family as 83 − 29 = 54?
items.e: Addition is the inverse of subtraction. 83 − 29 = 54, so 54 + 29 = 83. 83 + 29 = 112 is true, but it does not use 83, 29 and 54.

items.q: Which number sentence is in the same fact family as 720 − 450 = 270?
items.e: Addition is the inverse of subtraction. 720 − 450 = 270, so 270 + 450 = 720. 720 + 450 = 1 170 is true, but it does not use 720, 450 and 270.

items.q: Which number sentence is in the same fact family as 1 000 − 365 = 635?
items.e: Addition is the inverse of subtraction. 1 000 − 365 = 635, so 635 + 365 = 1 000. 1 000 + 365 = 1 365 is true, but it does not use 1 000, 365 and 635.

items.q: What is the missing number in the bar model?
items.e: The whole is the two parts added: 45 + 38 = 83. Not 73: that forgets to carry the ten from 5 + 8 = 13.

items.q: What is the missing number in the bar model?
items.e: The whole is the two parts added: 256 + 168 = 424. Not 88: that subtracts. Not 314: that forgets to carry both tens.

items.q: Which number sentence is not in the fact family of 54, 29 and 83?
items.e: The fact family of 54, 29 and 83 is 54 + 29 = 83, 29 + 54 = 83, 83 − 54 = 29, 83 − 29 = 54. 29 − 83 = 54 is not in it: the whole must come first: 83 − 29 = 54.

items.q: The pans balance, so 45 + 38 = 40 + ?. What is the missing number?
items.e: = means both sides have the same value. The left side is 45 + 38 = 83. So 40 + ? = 83 and ? = 43. Or: 40 is 5 less than 45, so ? must be 5 more than 38. Not 83: that is the value of the left side, not the missing number. Not 33: that changes 38 the wrong way.

items.q: The pans balance, so 27 + 56 = 30 + ?. What is the missing number?
items.e: = means both sides have the same value. The left side is 27 + 56 = 83. So 30 + ? = 83 and ? = 53. Or: 30 is 3 more than 27, so ? must be 3 less than 56. Not 83: that is the value of the left side, not the missing number. Not 59: that changes 56 the wrong way.

= means both sides have the same value. The left side is 68 + 25 = 93. So 70 + ? = 93 and ? = 23. Or: 70 is 2 more than 68, so ? must be 2 less than 25. Not 93: that is the value of the left side, not the missing number. Not 27: that changes 25 the wrong way.

items.q: The pans balance, so 72 − 28 = 74 − ?. What is the missing number?
items.e: Work out the side you know: 72 − 28 = 44. So 74 − ? = 44, and ? = 74 − 44 = 30. Both numbers move the same way to keep the same difference. Not 44: that is the value of the left side. Not 26: that moves 28 the wrong way.

items.e: Work out the side you know: 85 − 39 = 46. So 86 − ? = 46, and ? = 86 − 46 = 40. Both numbers move the same way to keep the same difference. Not 46: that is the value of the left side. Not 38: that moves 39 the wrong way.

Themba adds 45 and 38, then adds 9. He writes: 45 + 38 = 83 + 9 = 92. What is wrong?
items.e: = means both sides are the same. 45 + 38 is 83, but 83 + 9 is 92, so “45 + 38 = 83 + 9” is not true. Themba should write two number sentences: 45 + 38 = 83 and 83 + 9 = 92.

items.q: What does the = sign mean in 50 + 30 = 60 + 20?
c: Both sides have the same value
items.e: = means “is the same as”. 50 + 30 = 80 and 60 + 20 = 80, so both sides have the same value. It does not just mean “the answer comes next”.

items.q: Which equation has n = 6 as its solution?
items.e: Put 6 in place of n and work out each left side. 6 + 9 = 15, so n + 9 = 15 is true. The other equations are false when n = 6.

items.q: Which equation has n = 8 as its solution?
items.e: Put 8 in place of n and work out each left side. 4 × 8 = 32, so 4 × n = 32 is true. The other equations are false when n = 8.

items.q: Which equation has y = 12 as its solution?
items.e: Put 12 in place of y and work out each left side. 30 − 12 = 18, so 30 − y = 18 is true. The other equations are false when y = 12.

items.q: Which equation has k = 7 as its solution?
items.e: Put 7 in place of k and work out each left side. 42 ÷ 7 = 6, so 42 ÷ k = 6 is true. The other equations are false when k = 7.
Put 9 in place of n: 9 + 7 = 16. Both sides are equal, so yes, 9 is a solution.
7 − 8 does not give 15, so 7 is not a solution. 7 came from 15 − 8: subtracting instead of adding. Undo − 8 by adding: n = 15 + 8 = 23. Check: 23 − 8 = 15.
Put 8 in place of n: 5 × 8 = 40. Both sides are equal, so yes, 8 is a solution.
2 ÷ 3 is not 6, so 2 is not a solution. Undo ÷ 3 by multiplying: n = 6 × 3 = 18. Check: 18 ÷ 3 = 6.

Put 64 in place of n: 64 + 19 is 83, not 45. So 64 is not a solution. The solution is 26. Check: 26 + 19 = 45. 64 comes from adding 19 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: Andile’s book has 450 pages. He has read 178 pages. How many pages are left to read?
items.e: Number sentence: 178 + ? = 450. Use the inverse: ? = 450 − 178 = 272 pages. Check: 178 + 272 = 450. Not 628: that adds instead of subtracting.

items.q: The school tuck shop had 700 icy poles. After a hot week, 325 are left. How many icy poles were sold?
items.e: Number sentence: 700 − ? = 325. ? = 700 − 325 = 375 icy poles. Check: 700 − 375 = 325. Not 1 025: that adds the two numbers.

items.q: Two classes collect cans for recycling. Class 4A collects 45 cans on Monday and 38 on Tuesday. Class 4B collects 40 cans on Monday and the same total as 4A. Which number sentence shows 4B’s Tuesday cans?
items.e: The two totals are the same, so the two sides are equal: 45 + 38 = 40 + ?. 45 + 38 = 83, so ? = 43 cans.

items.q: Lindiwe works out 523 − 168 = 355. Which number sentence can she use to check her answer?
items.e: Check a subtraction with the inverse, addition: 355 + 168 = 523, so 355 + 168 = 523 shows the answer is right. 523 + 168 = 691 is true, but it does not check the subtraction.

items.q: Thabo’s family drives 640 km over two days of the holidays. They drive 285 km on the first day. How far do they drive on the second day?
items.e: Number sentence: 285 + ? = 640. ? = 640 − 285 = 355 km. Check: 285 + 355 = 640. Not 445: that takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column instead of regrouping.

items.q: A rainwater tank holds 900 ℓ. After watering the garden, 456 ℓ is left. Which number sentence shows how much water was used?
items.e: Start with 900 ℓ, take away an unknown amount, and 456 ℓ is left: 900 − ? = 456. Then ? = 900 − 456 = 444 ℓ.

items.q: A rainwater tank holds 900 ℓ. After watering the garden, 456 ℓ is left. How much water was used?
items.e: Number sentence: 900 − ? = 456. ? = 900 − 456 = 444 ℓ. Check: 900 − 444 = 456. Not 1 356: that adds the two numbers.

items.q: At the athletics day, Red House has 1 250 points and Blue House has 1 750 points. How many more points does Red House need to equal Blue House?
items.e: Number sentence: 1 250 + ? = 1 750. ? = 1 750 − 1 250 = 500 points. Check: 1 250 + 500 = 1 750. Not 3 000: that adds the two scores.

items.q: Bongani has to work out 38 + 245. He starts with 245 and adds 38. Which number sentence shows why that works?
items.e: You can add two numbers in any order and get the same total: 38 + 245 = 245 + 38.

items.q: At the fundraiser, the Grade 4 stall sells 46 sausages before school, 27 at break and 54 at lunch. How many sausages do they sell altogether?
items.e: Number sentence: 46 + 27 + 54 = ?. Add 46 + 54 first to make 100. Then 100 + 27 = 127 sausages. Not 100: that forgets the 27.

items.q: Naledi picks 14 apples at the orchard. Her brother picks some too. Together they have 32 apples. How many apples did her brother pick?
items.e: Equation: 14 + n = 32. n = 32 − 14 = 18 apples. Check: 14 + 18 = 32. Not 46: that adds instead of subtracting. Not 22: that takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: A teacher puts 24 chairs in 4 equal rows for an assembly. Let n be the number of chairs in each row. Which equation matches?
items.e: 4 rows with n chairs in each is 4 × n, and that is 24 chairs: 4 × n = 24. Then n = 6.

items.q: Each canoe holds 2 campers. There are 34 campers on the canoe trip. How many canoes do they need?
items.e: Equation: 2 × n = 34. n = 34 ÷ 2 = 17 canoes. Check: 2 × 17 = 34. Not 68: that multiplies. Not 32: that subtracts 2.

items.q: Pieter had n stickers. He gave 12 to friends and has 19 left. Which equation matches?
items.e: Start with n, give away 12, and 19 are left: n − 12 = 19. Then n = 19 + 12 = 31.

items.q: A school bus holds 48 learners. 29 learners are on the bus. How many more learners can get on?
items.e: Equation: 29 + n = 48. n = 48 − 29 = 19 learners. Check: 29 + 19 = 48. Not 77: that adds instead of subtracting. Not 21: that takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: A ringette team has 12 players. The coach can add n more players, but the team must have fewer than 18 players. Which inequality matches?
items.e: 12 players plus n more must be fewer than 18, so use <: 12 + n < 18. Not =: the team does not have to have exactly 18.

items.q: A ringette team has 12 players. The team must have fewer than 18 players, so 12 + n < 18. What is the greatest number of players the coach can add?
items.e: 12 + n < 18 gives n < 6. The greatest whole number less than 6 is 5. Check: 12 + 5 = 17 and 17 < 18. Not 6: 12 + 6 = 18, which is not fewer than 18. Not 30: that adds.

items.q: Amahle has read 9 books. To win a prize, she must read more than 14 books in all, so 9 + n > 14. What is the fewest more books she can read to win?
items.e: 9 + n > 14 gives n > 5. The least whole number greater than 5 is 6. Check: 9 + 6 = 15 and 15 > 14. Not 5: 9 + 5 = 14, which is not more than 14. Not 23: that adds.

items.q: 32 learners go on a field trip in 4 vans. Each van has the same number of learners. How many learners are in each van?
items.e: Equation: 4 × n = 32. n = 32 ÷ 4 = 8 learners. Check: 4 × 8 = 32. Not 28: that subtracts 4. Not 128: that multiplies.

items.q: Ayanda puts the same number of photos, n, on each of 5 pages of her scrapbook. She uses 30 photos. Which equation matches?
items.e: 5 pages with n photos on each is 5 × n: 5 × n = 30. Then n = 30 ÷ 5 = 6.
